title: Canonical minimum insertion/deletion diff
prompt:
Repair solve(payload), accepting {"a": [strings], "b": [strings]}. Return an ordered edit script of
{"op": "equal"|"delete"|"insert", "value": string} records that transforms a into b using the fewest
insertions plus deletions; equal costs zero. An equal/delete consumes the next a item; equal/insert
produces the next b item. The canonical rule is recursive: if the next items are equal, always emit
equal. Otherwise choose an operation permitting the minimum remaining edit count; when deletion and
insertion tie, choose deletion. Once one sequence ends, emit all remaining insertions or deletions.
There is no replacement operation. Include equal records in the result. Empty strings are normal items.

Do not mutate the input. Use only Python's standard library.

Public examples:
- Input: `{"a": ["x"], "b": ["x"]}`; output: `[{"op": "equal", "value": "x"}]`.
- Input: `{"a": ["a"], "b": ["b"]}`; output: `[{"op": "delete", "value": "a"}, {"op": "insert", "value": "b"}]`.

files.public_tests.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
import copy
import json
import unittest
from solution import solve

CASES = json.loads('[{"name": "equal", "input": {"a": ["x"], "b": ["x"]}, "expected": [{"op": "equal", "value": "x"}]}, {"name": "replace", "input": {"a": ["a"], "b": ["b"]}, "expected": [{"op": "delete", "value": "a"}, {"op": "insert", "value": "b"}]}]')

class PublicExamples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_examples(self):
        for item in CASES:
            with self.subTest(name=item["name"]):
                value = copy.deepcopy(item["input"])
                self.assertEqual(solve(value), item["expected"])
                self.assertEqual(value, item["input"], "solve must not mutate its input")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
